Restoring a removed output edge with a conv gains more than replacing an existing op (experiments 9 and 12).
Adding a conv on the direct input-to-output edge where none exists should help more than replacing an existing op.
Deleting a 3x3 conv edge loses a key path (experiment 10, -6 to -16), which hurts more than removing a weak op.

Replacing a 3x3 conv with pooling on a main path is very harmful (experiment 5, -17 to -23).
Downgrading a 3x3 conv to pooling loses parameters and accuracy (experiments 1 and 6).
Downgrading a 3x3 conv to a 1x1 conv reduces accuracy (experiment 20, -0.7 to -4.8).
With the output edge from node 2 missing, strengthening edge 4 matters more because it carries the node 1 route to the output (experiment 11).
